explanation: Chinese etiquette guides consistently describe feet as the 'lowest' part of the body, so deliberately showing the soles of your feet or pointing your feet at someone is considered disrespectful. This is treated less severely than in Thailand, where it intersects with Buddhist sacred-space rules, but it's still something hosts and etiquette guides flag as impolite.
local_tip: When sitting, especially with elders or hosts nearby, keep your feet flat on the floor or crossed at the ankle rather than propped up or pointed at anyone.
regional_note: Younger, more Western-influenced urban Chinese tend to be more relaxed about this than older or more traditional households.

also_check.note: Pointing feet at people or at Buddha images is a serious insult, since the foot is the lowest and head the highest part of the body.
Showing the soles of your feet is considered a clear sign of contempt.
Propping feet on furniture or toward others is seen as casual or rude in formal settings but isn't a major taboo.
